result:
**Opening argument for Debater A: c = 1/25**

The lower bound is a concrete construction. Take five parts V₁,…,V₅ of size n/5, join consecutive parts completely (a balanced blow-up of C₅), and inside each part place a sparse triangle-free graph with independence number o(n), such as a triangle-free Ramsey-type graph. The result is K₅-free: any clique uses at most two vertices per part, and two adjacent parts can contribute an edge each to form a K₄, but a fifth vertex would need to be adjacent to two vertices in one part, which triangle-freeness inside that part forbids. Its independence number is o(n), so it is admissible.

The graph has n²/5 cross edges. Since C₅ has max cut 4 of its 5 edges, any bipartition keeps at most 4n²/25 of them, so at least n²/25 edges must be deleted. Hence c ≥ 1/25.

For the matching upper bound, regularity shows the reduced graph R is triangle-free: a triangle of dense regular pairs, together with an edge inside a cluster (guaranteed by α = o(n)), yields a K₅. Deleting all within-cluster edges and using the optimal cut of R costs at most Φ(R)n² + o(n²). For C₅ with weights, every 2-coloring leaves a monochromatic edge, and AM–GM gives Φ ≤ 1/25 with equality at uniform weights. Checks on C₇, Petersen, Andrásfai graphs, and a six-vertex extension all stay at or below 1/25.

So the extremal structure is the C₅ blow-up, and c = 1/25.
